title: When the Ledger Burns Anew
premise: Estate lawyer Rafael Sterling is hired by a nervous client, Corinne Vale, who pays a retainer to prove that her brother's murder — scheduled in a will dated three days before his death — hasn't happened yet. As Rafael investigates the impossible document, he discovers the will was drafted from his own firm's templates and signed with his old partner's seal, implicating the man who vanished twelve years ago after a fire destroyed the town's land ledger. The killer is Judge Aldous Merrin, Rafael's mentor, who has been quietly rewriting ownership of Harrow's Bend through forged estates for decades; the 'future' murder is a trap to frame Rafael as the forger. In the climax, Rafael stages a fake reading of the burned ledger's reconstructed pages at the courthouse, baiting Merrin into confessing before the statute on the original fraud expires at midnight; Merrin is arrested, the true ledger surfaces, and Rafael burns his own twelve years of complicit filings to start clean.
about_author: Emrys Eastwick is the pen name of a former small-town court clerk who spent a decade handling probate files in coastal New England. Their debut novels are known for legal procedural precision and villains who hide inside institutions.

chapters.title: The Retainer
chapters.summary: Rafael Sterling's POV. A rain-soaked evening intake: Corinne Vale slides across an envelope of cash and a will dated three days before her brother Daniel's death, asking Rafael to prove no murder has occurred. The emotional beat is unease — Rafael recognizes the firm's own template paper and lies to her about it.

chapters.title: Filed Under V
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. He searches the firm's archives and finds the Vale file missing one page — the same page number torn from every estate he handled for Judge Merrin over twelve years. Flashbacks to the 2013 ledger fire surface. The beat is dread: the erasure is systematic, not accidental.

chapters.title: A Client Who Lies Well
chapters.summary: Corinne's POV. She admits she hired Rafael because investigators suspect her, and reveals Daniel had been blackmailing someone about land titles. Her grief curdles into calculation, and Rafael realizes she knows more than she's saying. Beat: shifting alliances, mutual suspicion laced with reluctant trust.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Hand
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Dinner with Judge Aldous Merrin, who quotes case law Rafael never taught him and mentions the Vale estate unprompted. Merrin warns him off 'sentimental archaeology.' The beat is corrupted loyalty — Rafael leaves honored and terrified in equal measure.

chapters.title: Ash and Alphabet
chapters.summary: Deputy Ilsa Moreno's POV. She reopens the 2013 fire as arson after finding melted filing-cabinet hinges matching Rafael's firm's cabinets. She interviews Rafael, who gives technically true answers. Beat: the hunter circling closer while the reader sees Rafael choosing each word like a man defusing wires.

chapters.title: What Daniel Knew
chapters.summary: Corinne's POV. She decodes Daniel's hidden notebook: parcels around Harrow's Bend changed owners through probate clerks' errors, all routed past Merrin's bench. Daniel's last entry names 'the reader.' Beat: revelation and guilt — Corinne realizes her blackmail funded her silence.

chapters.title: The Statute Clock
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. His junior partner is found unconscious after someone searched the vault; the fraud statute expires in nine days, after which every forged title becomes untouchable. Rafael decides to stop hiding and starts reconstructing the burned ledger from his own twelve years of filings. Beat: resolve hardening into strategy.

chapters.title: Bait in the File
chapters.summary: Rafael and Ilsa, uneasy allies, plant a fabricated ledger reconstruction in the courthouse records room, visible only to someone with judicial access. Someone takes the bait within hours. Beat: cat-and-mouse tension, the trap sprung but the identity of the hand still unproven.

chapters.title: Midnight Reading
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, climax. At a staged emergency probate hearing, Rafael reads the reconstructed ledger aloud as the statute tolls at midnight. Merrin, cornered by his own corrections to the forgery, argues the law like a mentor one last time — then confesses in open court when Rafael produces the torn pages. Beat: triumph shadowed by betrayal.

chapters.title: When the Ledger Burns Anew
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, resolution. Merrin awaits trial; Corinne inherits honestly and forgives Rafael imperfectly; Ilsa closes the arson case with Rafael's full statement, including his own complicity. In the final scene Rafael feeds his twelve years of protective filings into a burn barrel behind the office. Beat: costly absolution — truth kept, loyalty spent.
